security.summary: The advertised stage-only C# builder guard does not reject the approved main project on Windows.

logicerrors.summary: Canonical project path is compared to the noncanonical forward-slash ApprovedRoot literal, so both main-project refusal branches are false on Windows.
logicerrors.cause: MaterialsBuildPolicy.ValidateProject returns Path.GetFullPath(current), e.g. F:\[WORKSPACE]\[HERMES]\[CHATGPT]\PokemonThrowbackTCG. Admission and BuildWindows compare that result using project==ApprovedRoot, whose value uses forward slashes. ValidateProject deliberately accepts BOTH main and exact owned stage, so it does not enforce stage-only scope itself.
logicerrors.impact: With otherwise admitted output/settings, CreateBootstrap can pass Admission in the main Editor and proceed to NewScene/SaveScene/SaveAssets; BuildWindows can open the main scene and mutate main PlayerSettings before building. The Python staging driver is correctly scoped, but the exposed C# menu/execute-method entrypoints are not stage-only as required.
logicerrors.notClaimed: No main Editor, Unity build entrypoint, player, or live Saves directory was executed/opened to demonstrate this. The final historical native build did run from the correct stage and its evidence remains valid.
logicerrors.requiredBeforeApproval: Make the C# admission require the canonical exact owned stage (or compare canonical paths consistently), cover both entrypoints with a pre-mutation main-project rejection regression, and re-pin/rebuild/review the corrected source. No fix was made in this review.

testgaps.description: Existing BuildPolicyTests verify ValidateProject accepts main and stage but do not exercise the stage-only Admission guard. Thus the exact Windows separator mismatch escaped all policy/build/player tests.

The shader oracle verifies full texture bytes, actual masks and animated inside pixels. Its outside-pixel check inspects red only and omits a 2-pixel border; it is not an exhaustive visual/compositing proof. Both reviewed shader sources multiply alpha by mask.r*mask.a.

Demo invokes the focus-loss callback through SendMessage, rather than independently inducing an OS focus transition. Pause/error clock and AudioSource silence checks are real runtime assertions, not proof of audible output or human visual/hearing acceptance.
